Best time to visit Rishikesh: a month-by-month guide

📅 6 Oct 2026·⏱ 8 min read·By Geetu
Home / Journal / Best time to visit

We get this question on WhatsApp almost every day: "When should we come?" After five years of living here — watching the forest change colour from our terrace — here's the honest answer, month by month, with no tourism-brochure gloss.

Short answer: the best time to visit Rishikesh is late September to November (clear skies, big rafting water, comfortable days) and March to mid-June (warm, green, the river at full flow). Skip the July–September monsoon if you want rafting and treks, and pack warm layers for the cold, quiet December–February nights.

Rishikesh season by season

SeasonMonthsWeatherBest for
AutumnLate Sep–Nov22–30°C days, clear skiesRafting, swimming, first-timers
WinterDec–Feb8–20°C, cold nightsQuiet retreats, bonfires, deep rest
Spring/SummerMar–mid-Jun20–38°C, warmRafting, treks, escaping the plains
MonsoonJul–mid-SepHeavy rain, humidLush forest, lowest rates (no rafting)

Autumn (late September–November): the all-rounder

If you only remember one thing from this guide, remember this: October and November are the sweet spot. The monsoon has washed the air clean, the Ganga is still full and green from the rains, and rafting reopens with serious water. Days are warm enough for a swim and nights are cool enough to sleep under a blanket. It's also when the Himalayan peaks become visible on clear mornings. This is when most of our guests rebook for the following year before they've even left.

Winter (December–February): for the ones who want quiet

Rishikesh in winter is a different, gentler place. Fewer people, mist on the river in the mornings, and the kind of silence you came looking for. Days are mild and sunny; nights drop to single digits, so our bonfire gets lit most evenings and the kitchen leans into warm Garhwali food. Christmas to New Year is the one genuinely busy window — book well ahead. January is our most underrated month: peaceful, affordable, and perfect for a quiet winter escape.

Spring & summer (March–mid-June): green, full, and alive

Spring is when the valley turns properly green and the river hits full flow — rafting and cliff jumping are at their best. From mid-April, as the plains turn into an oven, families from Delhi and NCR drive up for the cool forest air. This is peak family season. It's also when the Char Dham Yatra begins, so the roads through Rishikesh get busier — plan an early start on travel days.

Monsoon (July–mid-September): beautiful, but know the trade-off

The monsoon forest is genuinely spectacular — everything is impossibly green and the waterfalls run hard. But the authorities suspend rafting for safety, some trek routes close, and landslide delays on the hill roads are real. If you come now, come for slowness: reading on the terrace, the smell of rain on the soil, and the lowest room rates of the year.

When we'd personally tell you to come

  • First time in Rishikesh? Mid-October to mid-November. You get everything working at once.
  • Want a quiet retreat? January or February — just bring warm layers.
  • Travelling with kids / parents? March–April or October, for the gentlest weather.
  • Here for rafting and adventure? October–November or April–May.
Whatever month you pick, the forest keeps its own calendar. Come once and you start reading it — which is usually when people decide to come back.
